extracted.intended_audience: NFL club executives, club communications staff, coaches, players, and accredited local media
extracted.subtask_description: Official NFL policy setting mandatory media-access requirements for clubs, coaches, players, and staff across gameday, practice week, training camp, minicamps, OTAs, and postseason. Specifies timing, location, privacy protections, role-specific availabilities, reporting requirements, and sanctions for violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-game access
rubrics_metrics.description: After a reasonable waiting period (defined as 10-15 minutes maximum after the completion of the game and the players have entered the locker room), the home and visiting locker room areas will be opened to accredited media for immediate access to all players for the sole purpose of conducting interviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clubs must bring the head coach, the quarterback, and at least one additional impactful player to an interview area near the locker room. Clubs must set up interview areas with a riser, microphones, and a camera platform; visiting team area must be adequate. Shower areas must be screened; clubs must supply wrap-around towels/robes and take other privacy measures. Training room and treatment areas off-limits. A club communications staffer must announce opening/closing, remain until media depart, and ensure accredited media are performing the job function granted. Name plates must remain until locker room clears. No on-field postgame player interviews before locker room opens (except league/club broadcast partners).

rubrics_metrics.name: Weekly regular-season media access (overall)
rubrics_metrics.description: Beginning no later than the week prior to the regular season through the playoffs, clubs will make players available during the normal practice week (based on a Sunday game) on Monday, Wednesday, Thursday and Friday; includes mandatory open locker room sessions for a minimum of 45 minutes on Wednesday, Thursday, and Friday.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monday availability may be open locker room, interview room, other location, or virtual; Tuesday treated as players' day off. Clubs may conduct open locker room interviews outside the locker room at club/player request but media must be allowed to request interviews in person in locker room. Clubs must ensure player privacy (screen showers, distribute appropriate clothing) and notify players before opening. The 45-minute period should occur when players are available; club responsibility to deliver access to all players and player responsibility to cooperate. Clubs may split open locker room into pre/post-practice windows (e.g., 30 and 15 minutes). A communications staffer must be present and announce closure at the end. If team gives two days off after a game, arrange for key players to be available on Monday.

rubrics_metrics.name: Head coaches availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Head coaches must be available consistently to the media that regularly cover the team, at least three days during each practice week from training camp through season end, and available to local media the day after all games either in person or remotely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If available three days only, those availabilities may not be on three consecutive days. Offensive/defensive/special teams coordinators must be available on a day the head coach is not speaking. At club's option, head coach may be made available to opposing team's media each week.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assistant coaches access
rubrics_metrics.description: Clubs must provide regular and reasonable access to assistant coaches (coordinators/assistant head coaches and all primary position coaches) through communications; assistant coaches may not be put off limits and clubs may not unreasonably withhold permission for them to speak to media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Passing/running game coordinators are treated as primary position coaches. Media access to assistant coaches on game day is a club decision; any game-day access is in addition to mandatory access rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinators weekly availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Offensive, defensive, and special teams coordinators must be available to media that regularly cover the club at least once between Monday and Friday during every practice week for a minimum of 10-15 minutes, beginning with the week leading to Week 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clubs must communicate scheduled availability to media in advance each week; media do not need to request weekly access. If no named coordinator exists (or head coach serves in that capacity), another position coach must fulfill obligation. If head coach is available three times during the practice week, coordinators must be available on a day head coach is not speaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assistant head coaches & primary position coaches availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Assistant head coaches and all primary position coaches must have regular access: at least two mandatory media availabilities during the club's offseason program (separated by at least 10 days) and bi-weekly availabilities beginning in August through the conclusion of the playing season for media that regularly cover the team.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure of sessions (single day or multiple days, in-person or remote) is a club decision. It is not permissible to deny other requests because of these mandatory availabilities. Assistant coaches must still be reasonably available outside these mandatory sessions.

rubrics_metrics.name: General managers/secondary football executives availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Club general managers and secondary football executives must each be available to the media at least twice yearly: once between the Scouting Combine and the week following the NFL Draft, and a second time either during training camp or following final roster reductions to 53 players.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition: secondary football executive refers to title of assistant general manager and/or next in line to primary football executive supervising Player Personnel. Availability responds to public interest in roster construction and development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Players availability and restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Players must be available to media following every game and regularly in person during the practice week as required under league rules and contracts; boycotts are not permissible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Players with unusually heavy media demands may be required to be available at least once during the practice week in addition to post-game availability (applies to maximum one or two players per team). Minimum for such players does not include other required obligations (network production meetings, national media interviews arranged by team).

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice access and injury reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Beginning Sept 1 and throughout regular season/playoffs, daily practice (Monday–Friday) must be open to local media for at least the first 30 minutes or until start of 'team' work. Clubs must designate on the NFL Injury Reporting Platform names of players who missed any portion of 11-on-11 team or individual work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clubs may limit videotaping/photographing of certain practice portions. Clubs set reasonable ground rules for coverage, balancing publicity and team goals. For practice sessions open to the public, clubs must allow reporting (tweeting, blogging) of newsworthy events (VIP visitors, exceptional plays, standout rookies).

rubrics_metrics.name: Field access limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Local media and broadcast television affiliates will not exceed 30 people with field access, of which 12 must be offered to the visiting team. Clubs may accredit between one and five local broadcast television video cameras on the sidelines to serve as the pool feed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These individuals count against the local media/broadcast allotment. Club in-house media and league media/partners are categorized separately. Access to pregame field area is a club decision subject to league/broadcast policies; postgame field access is subject to players/coaches departing the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: On-field media coordinator requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Each team must provide for each game an on-field media coordinator to help the televising network and other media in and around the field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinator should be located near the bench area during games with direct communication to the team's Communications Director in the press box.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibility of club officials for administering access
rubrics_metrics.description: Each club will assign two appropriate members of its communications staff to administer post-game and practice week media access policies; one or both must be present during media availabilities following each game and during the practice week.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designated officials ensure orderly postgame access, confirm media perform granted job functions, announce locker room closure, and remain until media depart.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal access principle
rubrics_metrics.description: All accredited media must be given access to designated player and coach interview times during the practice week, following games, and during training camp and minicamp.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a club allows media to attend daily practice, all members of the media who regularly cover the team must be admitted. Barring individual members of regularly accredited media for 'unfair coverage' or similar reasons is not permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media Access Plan submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Each club must provide complete details on the club's media access plan by Thursday, July 31, using a form provided by the league office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once received, league office will review. Clubs must acknowledge that the club president or GM, head coach, and communications director clearly understand media-related requirements of NFL policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offseason OTAs media access
rubrics_metrics.description: Clubs must open at least one of every three Organized Team Activity (OTA) days to the media; recommended to open the first OTA session of the year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On designated days teams must make the head coach and players available for interviews and open the OTA on-field session to media in its entirety (limited videotaping/photographing permissible). Mandatory OTA media sessions are in addition to veteran minicamps; access to Phase One/Two offseason workouts is a club decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory rookie minicamp access
rubrics_metrics.description: During a club's post-NFL Draft rookie minicamp (one of the two weekends following the Draft), local media must be provided at least one day of access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On designated day teams must make rookies available for interviews and open at least a portion of the on-field session to media. If entire on-field session is open it is permissible to limit videotaping/photographing certain portions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory veteran minicamp access
rubrics_metrics.description: During a club's mandatory veteran minicamp, all daily practices must be open in their entirety to local media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permissible to limit videotaping/photographing of certain portions. Players and the head coach must be available to the media for interviews each day during minicamp. Media access to rookie or voluntary minicamp is a club decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training camp access
rubrics_metrics.description: Beginning the first day of preseason training camp through August 21, all daily practices must be open in their entirety to local media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permissible to limit videotaping/photographing of certain practice portions. Players and head coach must be available regularly during preseason. One or two players with heavy demands may be made available to local media once per practice week (not including preseason game days). Assistant coaches must be available at least twice per month beginning in August. Joint workouts with other clubs must be open in their entirety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-draft news conference requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Every team is required to hold a pre-draft news conference with its head coach, and/or general manager, and/or player personnel director within two weeks of the draft.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose is to respond to fan interest in the draft and offseason squad development and to promote key league/club events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-season media requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Minimum regular-season practice week media access standards apply during the playoffs, with recommended supplemental availabilities due to increased interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clubs scheduling off days during a playoff bye week must make key players available. Clubs must comply with league office news conference schedule for playoff games; Conference Championship teams must adhere to committee-established media requirements (availabilities at least Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, head coach available each day, starting QB available Wednesday and one of Thursday/Friday). Super Bowl week arrangements communicated in advance and may differ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Season-ending news conference and locker room opening
rubrics_metrics.description: Every team is required to open the locker room for interviews the day after the season ends and hold a news conference during the week following the end of its season with head coach, and/or chief executive, and/or club president, and/or general manager.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose is to serve fan interest in the conclusion of the team's season.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medical information standards and concussion protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: Clubs must ensure all medical information issued to media is credible, responsible, and specific; in-game injury announcements must be specific to a body part, accurate, and updated as warranted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clubs are required to enter in-game injury information through the online Injury Reporting Platform (mobile accessible). Announce when players are being evaluated for possible concussion and update as soon as possible. A player diagnosed with a concussion will not be made available to media after the game until cleared by the Independent Neurological Consultant (INC). Clubs expected to update media on significant injuries during offseason/training camp/preseason. Injury reporting compliance governed by Integrity of the Game certifications from senior management. Super Bowl teams must submit injury report during bye week.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weekly depth chart requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Every team must produce a credible weekly depth chart for the media beginning no later than the week of its first preseason game and updated weekly through the end of the season.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depth chart must include the 11 offensive positions and 11 defensive positions considered base units, list expected starters and backups at each position. Listing players at each position in alphabetical order is prohibited. Clubs should include practice squad members on alphabetical and numerical rosters included on game day flipcards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availabilities with opposing team media (club option)
rubrics_metrics.description: At the club's option, the head coach and a key player may be available to the opposing team's local media each week.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communications directors may take requests from opposing team's media but decision to conduct availability is at club's discretion. Clubs will accommodate other appropriate media interviews upon reasonable request throughout the season.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team meeting on media & public/community relations
rubrics_metrics.description: Each club is required to hold a team meeting during training camp on media and public/community relations that the club president or general manager, coaches and communications staff must attend.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required items include playbook section on player media responsibilities, importance of good media/community relations, league and club policies (specifically open locker room sessions), and instructional materials (e.g., 'NFL Players and the Media' video) must be made available to players.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual media training requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Each club is required to conduct a media training session each year prior to the start of the regular season for all players and coaches, plus a separate session for rookies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Can be one session or separate sessions. League office will assist in identifying professional media trainers or advise clubs using their own staff. Mandatory training sessions are in addition to the training camp meeting reviewing league/club policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Club media & public relations brochure
rubrics_metrics.description: Each club will produce an annual brochure for coaches and players listing individual local media (with photos) and reviewing club policies on media and public/community relations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Brochure used as an educational/reference tool for coaches and players on local media contacts and policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press Will Call and parking accommodations
rubrics_metrics.description: Each club will have a separate Press Will Call window or booth, preferably at or near the Press Entrance, and should make credentials available at Press Will Call four hours prior to kickoff for preseason, regular-season and post-season games.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clubs should provide appropriate game-day parking accommodations to working media, include maps/parking info on passes, assist media with security escort to car after game, and provide rideshare pickup instructions on request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press box seating management
rubrics_metrics.description: Clubs will determine the number of individuals that have access to the press box and should exert best effort to limit the number of club personnel in the press box during games.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Club responsibility to control press box occupancy to preserve workspace for working media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Violations and enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Violations of the media access procedures will be considered conduct detrimental to the league and will be subject to league accountability measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Noncompliance may result in league sanctions; clubs are responsible for adherence to all policies described.
